sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

No information is available on the clinical use of lactulose during breastfeeding. Because lactulose is poorly absorbed orally, it is unlikely to reach the breastmilk in large amounts. Any lactulose that the infant absorbs from milk is rapidly eliminated in the urine. Some experts consider lactulose to be a laxative of choice during breastfeeding. Lactulose is unlikely to adversely affect the breastfed infant and no special precautions are required.
